# Independent finite-profile conformance review data

Issue [N0-07 #13](https://github.com/whoodes/namtab/issues/13) owns this bounded synthetic corpus. The [finite profile and state inventory](../../../docs/engine/compatibility-and-core.md#finite-n1-development-profile) own semantics. The [test policy](../../../docs/engineering/16-test-and-ci-strategy.md#terminal-conformance-and-real-interaction) owns qualification. Independent review is pending; these files do not accept NG0 or authorize N1 implementation.

`goldens.json` contains 26 hand-authored state traces, 24 input expectations and two pairs whose active cells, attributes and cursor match while hidden state differs. Every checkpoint explicitly records both grids, cell attributes, cursor, wrap, regions, tabs, ordinary saves, current attributes, input modes, return slot and parser continuation. Rows are literal width-one cell strings; unlisted attribute overrides use the explicit default cell attributes. Reply arrays are cumulative proposed effects through that checkpoint, with event-local ordinal identities. Input cases start independently at their stated mode cut after assumed valid broker admission; they exercise no broker, application or frontend.

The projection is deliberately specified in the JSON: it excludes allocator-specific row IDs, semantic revisions, diagnostic counters and authority/delivery records. It is not a complete snapshot or a proof of complete state equality. Future V08 must add full-inventory and relational row/anchor/counter assertions before certification. Goldens are authored from policy choices, never populated from an implementation's output. Mechanical authoring expanded repeated blank/default fields and encoded literal byte strings only. There is no VT parser, semantic reducer, snapshot loader or input encoder here.

`bounds.json` records exact profile caps, a CSI 512/513-byte boundary, a 65,536-byte discarded DCS payload and exact/over-bound input and geometry cases. Long payloads use finite literal-repeat recipes to keep review data bounded. Their expected cursor/cell/retention facts are explicit independent assertions. Static recipe arithmetic neither measures retained memory/work nor proves an engine enforces a cap. Allocation failure, work scheduling, diagnostic/identity saturation, history eviction and reply queue pressure still require the independent future runner below.

The six original X4 streams appear verbatim as new derivations at the original 5×12 geometry. Their independently authored private-profile expectations do not replace the historical serialized-state oracle. `manifest.json` pins exact repository paths and SHA-256 hashes for original shared inputs/manifest, original X4 oracle/result, EA1 continuation/alias/selection results and prior profile/state review data. Each derivation names its source record and exact source case ID. Classic Ctrl-I/M/[ input regressions name the corresponding EA1 case; named Tab/Enter/Escape counterparts are newly authored policy cases. A bounded EA1 continuation subreport can say PASS while historical selection remains FAIL. Original X4/EA1 bytes and FAIL verdicts remain immutable. Whole historical archive verification remains `make ea1-preservation`; this corpus does not replace it or rerun candidate engines.

Oracle review identified an ambiguity between “discard alternate contents” and retaining inactive grid-local state. The finite table now explicitly chooses **P-1049-exit-grid-local-reset**: 1049 exit blanks alternate cells with default attributes, resets its cursor/wrap/region/tabs/ordinary save and retires/reallocates its row identities; primary/history and restored session attributes/input modes survive. The dedicated transition changes alternate region/tabs/save/cursor/attributes before exit and asserts their reset afterward while application cursor mode survives. This is a clarified unadvertised draft policy, not a claim about universal xterm behavior, a changed accepted profile or an implemented result. Previous review data and historical bytes are unchanged.

All new values are synthetic: no recordings, prompts, secrets, user paths, environment dumps or embedded commands are executed. Existing sources retain their recorded provenance. No upstream source/corpus, Unicode data or license is copied or adopted, and no project license is added. S07/S08/S09 explain vocabulary in the contract; their moving pages are not content-pinned incorporated data. N0-08 owns any future upstream import/source/license decision. CI performs no network source lookup.

## Static checks and transport schedules

`node scripts/check-native-fixtures.mjs` verifies this corpus, its source pins, and the existing native identity/receipt/state/provenance manifests; it parses the earlier native-profile review file and verifies its new source pin. The existing `node scripts/check-fixtures.mjs` invokes it after the untouched shared manifest check. Checks reject duplicate JSON keys (including escaped duplicate spellings), unsafe or duplicate paths, escaping symlinks, unlisted native JSON payloads, payload/hash drift, missing coverage, invalid geometry/attributes/parser bounds, cap changes, corrupted chunks, historical stream edits, erased hidden distinctions and duplicate reply identities. These are static oracle/data consistency checks. A valid but semantically wrong in-bounds golden can pass them and must be found through independent contract/oracle review.

For each literal output event, all single byte cut offsets including zero/end are explicitly listed and validated. Every event of 1–8 bytes requires all `2^(n-1)` nonempty contiguous transport partitions. The checker enumerates their schedules and verifies reassembly; it does not feed a terminal implementation. Longer literal events retain every single cut plus explicit sample chunks. Recipes require every single cut and 64 seeded contiguous partitions, seed 1300711, bounded by 131,072 materialized bytes, 257 keeper events and ten seconds per future recipe run. These are future budgets, not measured times. Per-event transport variation preserves keeper event identity/order and the 512-byte event cap; short multi-event runners must compose schedules across those fixed events. A scheduling yield never becomes a new event. Zero/end cuts allow empty harness prefixes/suffixes, not zero-byte output events, EOF, final bytes or terminators.

A future comparison that changes keeper event segmentation must align semantic prefixes and compare cells/modes/continuation/effects under an explicit event-identity mapping. Event cuts, row IDs, revisions and reply identities cannot simply be asserted equal across different segmentation. Replay inspects proposed replies but dispatches zero effects. Real delivery, replay suppression, two-view authority and uncertain writes remain NOT RUN.

## Independent runner and oracle challenges required before V07–V11

| Family | Required independent runner and falsifiers | Current evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V07 | Separate byte-action model, all short partitions and all single cuts, numeric 65,535/65,536, five/six digits including zeros, 64/65 fields, ESC/CSI intermediate and total-length bounds, C0 accounting, cancel/restart/EOF, OSC/DCS/APC/PM/SOS discard and seeded malformed/long fuzz. Charge bytes/work, preserve seeds and minimized failures, test exact/one-beyond limits. Mutate ignored-final consumption, ignore precedence, UTF-8 prefix reprocessing and retained string payload. | Static metadata, shapes, partitions, recipe arithmetic and mutation rejection only; parser/fuzz NOT RUN. |
| V08 | Full hidden-state inventory and independent small-state model, exact-tuple continuation at every eligible cut, inactive grid/saves/return/tabs/regions/wrap and current attributes, reset/resize/history IDs/eviction, closed/unknown state. Remove one hidden field, flatten save slots, revive cropped cells or rewind identities. | Explicit two-grid subset goldens and equal-visible challenge pairs; state/restore NOT RUN. |
| V09 | Finite profile: CJK/combining output becomes one width-one replacement per scalar; corresponding text input refuses before write; resize crops without reflow or wide tails. Later advertised Unicode/grapheme/wide-cell/reflow profile needs pinned licensed Unicode data and independent occupancy/edit/resize oracle. | Static repertoire restrictions and refusal/replacement/crop expectations; Unicode/wide-cell certification NOT RUN and unadvertised. |
| V10 | Independent intent table covering every admitted named key/modifier subset and consumed/layout fact, keypad identities, classic aliases, all input modes and reset/buffer survival, paste policy/caps/delimiter rejection, unsupported phases/enhancements. Run through both clients and admitted native API; remove a modifier or infer a physical/NumLock fact to ensure rejection. | Bounded byte/refusal examples only; actual encoder, exhaustive key coverage and clients NOT RUN. |
| V11 | Independent query/effect model: exact state cut/order/ordinals, equal and split queries, all selected query rows and unsupported no-reply cases, 128-reply/4,096-byte reservations, two views/reconnect producing zero extra replies, effect-free replay, crash/unknown delivery without resend. Mutate dedupe, duplicate reply writer, query state cut, reply order, event reservation and replay dispatch. | Exact proposed-byte examples and identity/size checks; actual reply dispatch/replay/crash/queue conformance NOT RUN. |

Compare future implementations with explicitly pinned xterm, Ghostty, VTE/parser sources and selected real terminal/version tuples only after source/license review. Classify a disagreement as a standard requirement, deliberate profile difference, implementation bug, reference bug or unresolved; include exact bytes, policy/version/geometry, source IDs, observations and reviewer rationale. Never use a vote or normalize a cursor/mode/reply discrepancy to green a case. The manifest classifies existing historical/profile differences; no new reference comparison was executed.

`tests/system/native-fixtures.test.mjs` changes cells/hashes, previous native payloads, rows/cursors, advertised repertoire, byte cuts/chunks, historical streams, hidden distinctions, reply identities, refusal bytes, caps, bounded recipes and source/path metadata. Several mutations recompute file integrity first so rejection must come from independent structural/coverage/budget rules. These passing mutation tests only show that the static checker rejects those corruptions. Future engine mutations above must be killed by independent state/effect oracles; generating goldens from the mutated or baseline implementation is forbidden. Correct an oracle only after contract review and an explained provenance update, never by blanket regeneration.
